nodes.summary: The de Bruijn multigraph of `s` (Pevzner–Tang–Waterman 2001) as its list of edge occurrences: one edge per `k`-mer occurrence, in order of position.
nodes.title: De Bruijn multigraph of a string

nodes.summary: The edge of the de Bruijn multigraph contributed by a `k`-mer `w`: from its prefix `(k-1)`-mer `w.dropLast` to its suffix `(k-1)`-mer `w.tail`.
nodes.title: De Bruijn edge of a k-mer

nodes.summary: Executable form of `kmers`: the suffixes of `s` are generated once by `List.tails`, so the cost is `O(|s| · k)` rather than the `Θ(|s|²)` of recomputing `s.drop i` for every `i`. The compiler uses it in place of `kmers` (`kmers_eq_kmersImpl`).
nodes.title: Efficient executable computation of k-mers

nodes.summary: Every Eulerian trail spells a string with the same `k`-mer multiset (`2 ≤ k`): if `W` is a walk of `(k-1)`-mers whose steps are a permutation of the edge occurrences of the de Bruijn multigraph of `s`, then the `k`-mers of the spelled string are a permutation of those of `s`. (The empty walk is allowed: it is a trail only when `s` has no `k`-mers, and spells `[]`.)
nodes.title: Every Eulerian trail spells a string with the same `k`-mer multiset

nodes.summary: The `k`-mers of `s` in order of position: the length-`k` windows `(s.drop i).take k` for `i + k ≤ |s|`.
nodes.title: The k-mers of a string

nodes.summary: The `(k-1)`-mer walk of `s` spells `s` back (`2 ≤ k`, `k - 1 ≤ |s|`).
nodes.title: The (k-1)-mer walk of a string spells the string

nodes.summary: The string spelled by a walk of `(k-1)`-mers: the first vertex followed by the last letter of each later vertex.
nodes.title: String spelled by a walk of (k-1)-mers

nodes.summary: The `k`-mer walk of `s` is an Eulerian trail of its de Bruijn multigraph: its steps are a permutation of the edge occurrences, each traversed once.
nodes.title: The `k`-mer walk of `s` is an Eulerian trail

nodes.summary: Its steps are exactly the edges contributed by the `k`-mers of `s`, one per occurrence, in order of position.
nodes.title: The `(k-1)`-mer walk of `s` traverses the de Bruijn multigraph in order

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
